## Purpose

<!-- hand:purpose -->
> Draft — owner review pending.

The alarm system: what the monitor has measured (displayed numerics, QRS detections, beat classes, sensor states) is
turned into alarm conditions, and each alarm is then taken through its life — delay, priority, raise, clear, latching,
acknowledge, silence and pause — under the active skin's rules and message text. It imitates IEC-style and Saadat-like
monitor conventions for teaching; it is not a certified alarm system. A clinician-educator can see why an alarm fires,
waits or stays quiet; an embedding developer gets one `alarmStatus` summary for the renderer (`l3/alarms/manager.ts`).
<!-- /hand:purpose -->

## Equations in words

<!-- hand:equations -->
> Draft — owner review pending.

- Conditions are a pure function of the observed data; a displayed numeric older than 5 s raises nothing, NIBP excepted
  because it is episodic (`l3/alarms/conditions.ts`).
- A condition must hold continuously for its delay before the alarm is raised, e.g. desaturation below 80 % for 20 s
  (`l3/alarms/conditions.ts`, `l3/alarms/manager.ts`).
- Arrhythmias: VF is recognised after 3 s; extreme bradycardia and tachycardia sit 20 bpm beyond the HR limits, clamped
  at 40/200 (adult) or 50/240 (neonate); a ventricular run ends after 2 s without a ventricular beat; a PAUSE alarm
  stays at least 5 s (`l3/alarms/conditions.ts`).
- Chaining: an active condition suppresses the ones it explains (asystole over VF/VT over VT over extreme rate over the
  HR limit; one apnoea instead of RR, awRR and EtCO2 low); a suppressed alarm is cleared, never latched (Philips
  chaining, [S2] IFU p. 99; `l3/alarms/conditions.ts`).
- An arterial line that is non-pulsatile with a mean below 10 mmHg for 5 s is a disconnection ([S2] p. 44;
  `l3/alarms/conditions.ts`).
- Priority levels are 1 high, 2 medium, 3 low; an alarm clears when its condition goes unless it is latched; under
  'lethal' latching the lethal arrhythmias (asystole, VF, VT, extreme rates) latch visually until acknowledged, and
  INOPs never latch (research/05 §6; `l3/alarms/manager.ts`).
- Acknowledge clears latched alarms and silences live ones; a new alarm of higher priority ends a silence or a pause
  (`l3/alarms/manager.ts`).
- Message text follows the skin, `***SpO2 94<96` style or Saadat-like uppercase English such as "HR TOO LOW"; texts no
  source quotes are inferred from those patterns (`l3/alarms/text.ts`).
<!-- /hand:equations -->
